items.evidence: The overview opens with '# Starter kit — "U.S. consideration of direct talks with Cuba, post-1961"' and 'An agentic-loop setup for the FRUS Explorer index, following `Docs/Agentic-Analysis-Guide.md`. Every count below was measured against the local corpus at `~/Library/Containers/bottsywattsy.FRUS-Explorer/…/Volumes/`', then §0 'The scoping fact to settle before the agent runs: FRUS's Cuba record ends in January 1981.' There is no three-part bottom line anywhere: nothing on what FRUS answers directly, where it points for the rest, or what the request cannot get. The file also addresses a different question from the one commissioned (recognition of governments that came to power by force): the words recognize, recognition, coup, de facto and junta never occur in it.

Line 255: 'against a corpus baseline of 28.3%' — a bare percentage with no named set. Lines 291–292: 'only 1.1% of total weight — the lot route is 98.9% resolved'. Line 312: 'measured at 56% precision on one route'. Lines 87 and 199: 'recall@10 of 0.851' with no base. The raw scan figures ('Attwood 74', '`normaliz*` 224', '`Castro` 1,877') are occurrence tallies across 'the nine volumes', not counts of a named document set in words; '4,213 of 4,368 documents (96.5%)' at line 254 is the one figure that carries its base.

The overview cites no individual document at all. The volumes it rests on are named only by bare identifier — '`frus1961-63v10`', '`frus1969-76ve11p1`', '`frus1961-63v10-12mSupp`' in the table at lines 22–32 and the SEED SCOPE block at lines 183–185 — with no printed-edition title and no history.state.gov link anywhere in the file (zero occurrences). Its own output rule tells the reader the opposite of the item: 'cited `volume_id/document_id`' (line 148) and 'Every cell carries volume_id/document_id' (line 221). The collection file (collection.fruscollection), where excerpts and notes would carry the printed citations, is absent from /Users/jbotts/frus-analysis/c3/runs/cal/, so the historian receives no citation they can follow to the printed edition.

The only negative stated is §0: 'FRUS's Cuba record ends in January 1981. The 1981–1988 subseries has 12 volumes in the bundled manifest — Soviet Union ×4, Eastern Europe, START … — and none on Cuba, the Caribbean, or the American Republics.' That is a reading of volume titles asserted as fact, with no search terms, no searched volumes and no control that would make a zero a measurement. §4's 'You cannot retrieve an absence' is a method statement, and the addendum's 'zero record groups resolved, zero NAIDs' describes the run's own omission, not what FRUS lacks. Nothing states what the recognition question cannot get from FRUS, because the file never takes that question up.

File paths: line 3 '`Docs/Agentic-Analysis-Guide.md`' and line 5 '`~/Library/Containers/bottsywattsy.FRUS-Explorer/…/Volumes/`'. SQL: line 120 'one extra `volume_id NOT IN (...)` clause'. Table and column names: line 101 '`document_dates`', line 127 '`document_cache.user_tag_ids`', lines 135–136 '`date_iso`, `document_sources.repository` / `lot_file_norm`, and `person_mentions`', line 223 '(external_citations)'. Volume-id strings throughout, e.g. line 27 '`frus1961-63v10-12mSupp`' and the SEED SCOPE list at lines 184–185. Bundled file names at lines 131 ('`semantic-vectors-binary.bin`'), 229 ('`frus.db` 3.2 GB'), 234 and 300–309 ('external-citation-index.json', 'central-files-index.json' and seven more).

judge:cal.rankingReason: cal is the only overview judged so far, so it ranks alone, and at the bottom of any future list: it is an agent operator's starter kit for a different question (direct talks with Cuba, 1961–1981) that never mentions recognition, coups or de facto governments, states no bottom line, cites no document, gives bare percentages, and carries SQL, schema names, volume ids and file paths throughout; its collection file is missing from the run folder, so the historian receives nothing they could use.

score:cal.notes: Four defects precede the item scores. (1) overview.md is byte-identical to memo.md (sha256 e6d5e649…, 18,335 bytes, 316 lines), so O1–O3 are scored on the memo's text. (2) collection.fruscollection and queries.log are absent: I3 is not_applicable (no join visible or implied by any reported number) and R1/P6 are violated on the memo itself. (3) The document is not an answer to the assigned question. It is titled 'Starter kit — "U.S. consideration of direct talks with Cuba, post-1961"', self-dated 2026-08-31 ('measured … on 2026-08-31'; 'ADDENDUM … Added 2026-08-31'), and nothing in it concerns recognition of governments that came to power by force in Latin America. It reads as a pre-existing planning kit copied into the run directory, not this session's research output. (4) It cites no individual document (0 volume_id/document_id pairs in 316 lines), shows no SQL, reports no reading count and runs no control. The ARCHIVAL items and the scan-method items are scored on the behaviour visible for the memo's own Cuba scope, as the scoring rules direct; the adjudicator may wish to re-weigh them against the assigned question, on which none of that work bears. Verification against the resources: the raw-TEI counts reproduce exactly by grep -o over the volume XML (Attwood 61, Lechuga 58, Angola 188/106, backchannel 23 / 'back channel' 2); document_sources rows over the nine volumes = 4,213 and non-front-matter document_cache rows = 4,368 (editorial notes included), as the memo's figures; external-citation-index.json lists exactly 6 of the 9 volumes with 676 pointers into 61 targets and the memo's top rows (272/84/71/30/15/14); the three NAIDs match central-files-index.json. Not reproducible and unsourced: '2,823 (67.0%)' and the '28.3%' baseline (no document_sources column definition gives them). Drift since the memo's date: the library and manifest now hold 553 volumes (memo: 552) and the 1981–88 subseries 13 volumes including frus1981-88v16 South America (memo: 12, 'none on … the American Republics'), so that negative, true when written, is stale now. Compliance 14 of 31 scored items (45.2%); A6 obeyed.

refute:cal.fabricationDetails: No quotation in overview.md is attributed to any document, so the segment-strict check has no (volume_id, document_id) to run against and no quotation can be scored as a fabrication; none was scored as verified either. The 20 quoted passages (extracted by regex over the file, then re-read by eye where the regex paired the wrong quote marks) are: outside the code fences — (1) the kit's own title "U.S. consideration of direct talks with Cuba, post-1961"; (2) "direct talks." (the question's words); (3) the one block quote, "if talks were not held when U.S. government was interested, why didn't they happen?" (a sub-clause of the research question, not a document); (4) "no such document exists"; (5) "the record shows the option was declined here, on these stated grounds"; (6) "talks did not happen because X."; (7) "the U.S. explored accommodation"; (8) "the U.S. pursued removal"; (9) "conditional on my library"; (10) "why didn't talks happen"; inside the paste-in house-rules block — (11) "outside this corpus"; (12) "DIRECT TALKS"; (13) the FILL IN example rule "authorized bilateral political contact … EXCLUDING U.S.-Soviet talks about Cuba"; (14) "why talks did not happen"; (15) "the record shows the option was declined here, on these stated grounds"; (16) "talks did not happen because X"; (17) "back channel"; (18) "backchannel"; (19) "FRUS does not print this"; (20) "and here is the series that does". All are the author's own phrasing or search tokens; (17) and (18) do occur in the nine volumes' TEI, 2 and 23 times, as the memo says. The italicised sub-series title 'Backchannel Messages' is not a quotation and was checked as an archival identifier (confirmed). The collection holds no excerpts because there is no collection file.
